content:
The possible multiplicative partitions of \(861=3\cdot 7\cdot 41\) into factors \(>1\) are:
\[
(861),\ (3,287),\ (7,123),\ (21,41),\ (3,7,41).
\]
For each factor \(m=a_i n+1\), we need \(n\mid m-1\).

- \((861)\): \(n\mid 860\), but no prime \(p\) gives \(n=p^{860/n}\).
- \((3,287)\): \(n\mid \gcd(2,286)=2\), so \(n=2\), impossible with exponents \(1,143\).
- \((7,123)\): \(n\mid \gcd(6,122)=2\), so \(n=2\), impossible with exponents \(3,61\).
- \((3,7,41)\): \(n\mid \gcd(2,6,40)=2\), so \(n=2\), impossible with exponents \(1,3,20\).
- \((21,41)\): \(n\mid \gcd(20,40)=20\). Testing divisors of \(20\), \(n=20\) gives exponents
\[
a_1=\frac{21-1}{20}=1,\qquad a_2=\frac{41-1}{20}=2.
\]
Then
\[
20=5^1\cdot 2^2,
\]
so \(n=20\) works.

Check:
\[
20^{20}=(2^2\cdot 5)^{20}=2^{40}\cdot 5^{20},
\]
so
\[
d(20^{20})=(40+1)(20+1)=41\cdot 21=861.
\]

\[
\boxed{20}
\]
